security_audit.summary: Most supplied alerts are benign documentation, integrity hashes, regex matches, or expected local build operations. Unconfined paths and active-content rendering expose untrusted projects; no evidence found of deliberate exfiltration or audit-directed prompt injection in reviewed material. The oversized executable bundle and 791 omitted matches remain review gaps, so these verdicts do not establish complete publication safety. Static review was capped at 400/1191 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 791 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: SVG and companion-file paths can escape project asset folders.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve paths and symlinks before reading, then enforce containment in designated asset and diagram folders. Add absolute-path and traversal regression tests.

remediation.issue: Active HTML and SVG content execute before QC.
remediation.suggestion: Disable document JavaScript, sanitize HTML and SVG, escape interpolated content, and deny network requests. Validate sources before browser rendering.

remediation.issue: Outline chapter paths are not confined to chapters.
remediation.suggestion: Reject absolute paths and require resolved chapter paths, including symlink targets, to remain within the project's chapter folder.

remediation.issue: Style selection can resolve token files outside the styles directory.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only registered style names. Enforce resolved containment in styles for production builds and keep test overrides explicit.

remediation.issue: The executable vendor bundle and omitted static matches remain incompletely reviewed.
remediation.suggestion: Compare the full vendor bundle against a reproducible build from locked dependencies. Review all 791 omitted matches before automatic publication.

semantic_findings.description: Raw Markdown HTML and unescaped callouts enter the Chromium PDF renderer. Authored SVGs enter page.setContent after only narrow external-reference checks. content.user_title: Create Korean Ebook PDFs from Topics or Manuscripts
content.value_statement: Preparing a Korean PDF book requires consistent content structure, typography, and pagination. Bookforge combines six design styles with guided writing, local rendering, automated quality checks, and visual review.
actual_capabilities: Guide topic research and chapter drafting, or normalize Markdown, text, and DOCX manuscripts without intentionally rewriting their meaning.
Apply practical, insight, academic, essay, business, or magazine styles using Typst or HTML rendering.
Generate covers, numbered contents, chapter openers, running elements, copyright pages, and PDF bookmarks.
Render AntV diagram sidecars and normalize authored SVG diagrams with font, palette, contrast, and label checks.
Check PDF dimensions, embedded fonts, text collisions, pagination, contents alignment, and callout consistency before promoting drafts to final output.
Generate page previews and contact sheets for visual review, and search small spacing adjustments with the refit tool.
limitations: Requires Python dependencies and Typst 0.14.x for Typst styles. HTML styles and diagram rendering also require Node.js, global Playwright, and Chromium.
HWP ingestion is unsupported. DOCX requires python-docx, and original formatting is normalized rather than reproduced exactly.
Quality checks do not independently verify factual accuracy, publication rights, or legal compliance. Human review of sources and rendered pages remains necessary.
Untrusted projects can exploit path and active-content risks. Use trusted inputs and isolated rendering; the vendor bundle remains incompletely reviewed.

best_practices: Keep book projects outside the skill repository and provide only trusted manuscripts, metadata, and SVG assets.
Choose a style for the audience and supply verified sources, image permissions, and substantive content for the selected length.
Run the build and QC gates, then inspect the cover, contents, chapter opener, and body pages before distributing the PDF.
anti_patterns: Do not process unknown projects or active HTML and SVG inputs with unrestricted browser or filesystem access.
Do not add filler chapters, excessive spacing, or forced page breaks merely to reach a page target.
Do not weaken gates to hide book defects or treat an uninspected draft as final output.

faq.question: Can I start with only a topic?
faq.answer: Yes. Topic mode guides research, outline planning, and chapter writing before typesetting and quality checks.

faq.question: Which manuscript formats are supported?
faq.answer: Markdown, text, and DOCX are supported inputs. DOCX requires python-docx; convert HWP to a supported format first.

faq.question: Which design styles are available?
faq.answer: The six styles are practical, insight, academic, essay, business, and magazine. Their trim sizes and layout engines differ.

faq.question: Does every style require Chromium?
faq.answer: No. Practical, academic, essay, and business use Typst. Insight, magazine, and diagram rendering require Playwright and Chromium.

faq.question: Does passing QC guarantee publication readiness?
faq.answer: No. QC checks defined layout and consistency rules. You must still inspect pages and verify facts, rights, and publication requirements.

faq.question: Can it safely render an unknown book project?
faq.answer: Not currently. The audit identified unconfined paths and active-content risks. Use trusted inputs and isolated rendering until those issues are addressed.
